# Numerical semigroups generated by arithmetic progressions

2 results, all proved, quoted from [Deicyde/atlas-lean](https://github.com/Deicyde/atlas-lean) at commit [035e1808](https://github.com/Deicyde/atlas-lean/tree/035e1808ca0c8983682b74153a02628d616d77ce); [its page on the ATLAS site](https://deicyde.github.io/atlas-lean/roadmap/NumberTheory/numerical-semigroups/numerical-semigroups-generated-by-arithmetic-pro/index.html).

## Tripathi's pseudo-Frobenius formula without assuming $d > 0$

Let $a$, $h$ and $k$ be
positive integers and $d$ a natural number with $\gcd(a, d) = 1$, and let $q$ and $r$ be natural
numbers with $1 \le r \le k$ and $a - 1 = qk + r$. Let $S$ be the set of all sums
$c_0 a + \sum_{i=1}^{k} c_i (ha + id)$ with natural numbers $c_0, \dots, c_k$. Then the natural
numbers $y \notin S$ such that $y + s \in S$ for every nonzero $s \in S$ are exactly the numbers

$$y = ha \left\lfloor \frac{x - 1}{k} \right\rfloor + (h - 1)a + dx$$

with $x$ a natural number satisfying $a - r \le x \le a - 1$.

The hypotheses force $d > 0$: if $d = 0$, then $\gcd(a, d) = a = 1$, and $a - 1 = qk + r$ with
$r \ge 1$ is impossible.

Formalized by `MetaMathlibExt.tripathi_pseudo_frobenius_arithmetic_progression_general`, a theorem declared in [MathlibExt/NumberTheory/TripathiPseudoFrobenius.lean, line 366](https://github.com/Deicyde/atlas-lean/blob/035e1808ca0c8983682b74153a02628d616d77ce/MathlibExt/NumberTheory/TripathiPseudoFrobenius.lean#L366). [Its page on the ATLAS site](https://deicyde.github.io/atlas-lean/roadmap/NumberTheory/numerical-semigroups/numerical-semigroups-generated-by-arithmetic-pro/index.html#tripathi-pseudo-frobenius-arithmetic-pro).

## Tripathi's pseudo-Frobenius formula

Let $a$, $d$, $h$ and $k$ be positive integers with
$\gcd(a, d) = 1$, and let $q$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $1 \le r \le k$ and
$a - 1 = qk + r$. Let $S$ be the set of all sums $c_0 a + \sum_{i=1}^{k} c_i (ha + id)$ with
natural numbers $c_0, \dots, c_k$, that is, the additive monoid generated by
$a, ha + d, \dots, ha + kd$. Then the natural numbers $y \notin S$ such that $y + s \in S$ for
every nonzero $s \in S$ are exactly the numbers

$$y = ha \left\lfloor \frac{x - 1}{k} \right\rfloor + (h - 1)a + dx$$

with $x$ a natural number satisfying $a - r \le x \le a - 1$.

The case $a = 1$ cannot occur, since then $a - 1 = qk + r$ with $r \ge 1$ is impossible. When
$k \ge a$, these numbers are exactly $(h - 1)a + dx$ for $1 \le x \le a - 1$.

## Sources

- Amitabha Tripathi, "The Frobenius Problem for Modified Arithmetic Progressions," Journal of Integer Sequences 16 (2013), Article 13.7.4, Theorem, lines 235–238, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL16/Tripathi/trip22.tex It follows from `tripathi_pseudo_frobenius_arithmetic_progression_general`; the hypothesis `hd` is unused and keeps the source's shape.
